verdict.rationale: Community reports show PostHog ships a docker deploy command and a posthog/posthog:latest image, so a self-hosted deployment exists. One user found it easy to get running; another found the production image created no database. Nothing in the pack documents self-hosting the feature-flag platform specifically, its open-source license, or keeping flag evaluation data on your own infrastructure. Missing for 10: first-party self-hosting docs, explicit open-source license or distribution evidence, confirmation that flags are included in self-hosted builds, documented local flag evaluation and data residency, recent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I can self-host the full flag platform from an open-source distribution, keeping evaluation data on my infrastructure

citations.quote: A user tried the docker deploy command from the landing page and found it "super easy to get up and running."
the production Dockerfile and posthog/posthog:latest image
